segments.text: Hot take, you're probably using the sauna wrong, and I was too. After over 200 sauna sessions, I learned I was making a huge mistake. Your goal in the sauna is not to sweat, it's to get your core body temperature to 102.4° F. When your body hits that temperature, it releases heat shock proteins. These protect brain function, metabolism, and cellular longevity. But you miss these benefits if you're not hitting that core body temperature. To find out if I was crossing this threshold, I had two options. One, swallow a pill that measures my core body temperature. Two, a rectal probe.

I chose the pill. And it turns out my 20-minute protocol just wasn't cutting it. In fact, it took me 31 minutes at 200° F to cross that threshold. In other words, it feels like you're dying. Now, here's the good news. My previous 20-minute sauna sessions still delivered many benefits. But if you want the real longevity benefits of sauna, your core body temperature needs to reach 102.4° F. The key to getting the most out of my sauna was to just let me cook.
